result.title: AxE: Benchmarking Agent-Environment Generalization of Video World Models via Grounded Events
result.summary: Edge cases are not the long tail; they are the norm. An embodied system deployed across changing environments, bodies, objects, and tasks will routinely encounter combinations that were absent from its training data. General-purpose physical intelligence therefore requires world models that reuse prior knowledge, predict consequences, and adapt with little or no additional training. Yet current evaluations of conditional video generation emphasize visual quality, prompt alignment, or isolated physical plausibility, leaving systematic generalization difficult to measure. We introduce AxE Bench, a benchmark that organizes condition changes along eight factors of the acting agent and of its environment, and pairs every original condition with controlled variants that change one side or both. WBench-plus applies the same structure to an existing multi-turn benchmark, pairing each WBench scenario with variants on the environment side, through its world setting or camera behavior, or on the agent side, through its interaction instructions. Additionally, to score generated futures, we develop an evaluation harness that combines vision-language reasoning with targeted computer-vision evidence, converting each video into temporally localized events and comparing generated events with reference events in both time and semantics. We summarize each model with the AxE Score, event Fidelity weighted by its Stability across original-variant pairs. Across twenty models, generated events match reference events far more often in timing than in content: no model exceeds a Fidelity of 13.01, the highest Stability is 0.55, and the highest AxE Score is 7.10. Together, these components turn world-model generalization from an informal aspiration into a falsifiable evaluation program for real and simulated interactions. Our project website can be found at: AxEBench.github.io

AI.brief_summary: AxE Bench 沿智能体与环境八个因素构造受控变体（并扩展 WBench 为 WBench-plus），再提出把生成视频解析为时间定位事件、与参考事件在时序和语义上比对的评测流程，以 Fidelity×Stability 得到 AxE Score，系统衡量视频世界模型的泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「事件级、时序与内容分离」的评分方式可能可供核查用于判断 latent 推理是否真正使用了视觉证据，原始-变体配对设计也可为泛化评价提供参照；但研究对象是条件视频生成的未来预测，与 VLM 内部推理状态和 latent 生成无直接关系。
